conclusion: No clear malware indicators found in the first-party paths reviewed. Bounded static review, not certification of all dependencies or binary equivalence. Release-to-main differences affect only guides and skills, not reviewed runtime/build code.

findings.finding: TSX is executable trusted code, with file/environment access and a subprocess bridge. Offline mode is not an OS sandbox.
Skill installation changes persistent agent configuration, installs hooks, and registers unpinned uvx mcp-for-blender.
Optional model setups download unpinned Git/Hugging Face/Python dependencies.
Optional app-host loopback MCP server exposes actions without visible Origin/Host/auth checks.
Release Actions use major tags rather than immutable SHA pins; Cargo/Bun lockfiles and release provenance are positive controls.
Local logs include command arguments, paths, hardware and errors. No transmission found in trace implementation.

limitations: Remote curl-to-shell installer not reviewed or used
Checksum verified against GitHub API digest; provenance attestation not independently verified
No guarantee a prebuilt binary matches source
